expected: A post-start canonical event is not forced into an already-running campaign.
Persisted campaign consequences remain authoritative even when later screen canon differs.
Procedural generation cannot overwrite a canon-reserved entity/location valid for the campaign date.
Unreserved space may be procedurally enriched.
Existing entity state is loaded rather than regenerated.
Generator rule changes do not silently rewrite materialized entities.
Renaming an entity preserves its stable ID, history and linked state.
Two entities may not become the same entity merely because their visible names match.
Adding a new unrelated subsystem does not change existing identity/personality/relationship outputs.
Derived seeds include campaign seed, stable entity ID, subsystem key and rules version.
Rules-version changes use keep-persisted, explicit migration or new-saves-only regeneration.
Silent regeneration of existing persistent entities fails validation.
INFERRED and GAME_ADDITION claims remain distinguishable from SCREEN_CANON.
Authority and confidence are represented as separate concepts.
Sensor, tricorder, dialogue or AI requests cannot spawn the fact they are querying.
Knowledge changes after observation while ground truth remains independently authoritative.
Generic persistence/identity semantics are not duplicated as setting-specific Star Trek rules without justification.
Trek-specific canon, species, organizations and technology remain in the Star Trek layer.
Gameplay-relevant lore cannot be marked complete without game-facing rules/data where applicable.
Persistent/generated domains declare identity, seed, persistence, versioning and validation behavior.
